newsitem.title: THAILAND: Burma says won't allow large group at Suu Kyi home.
newsitem.headline: Burma says won't allow large group at Suu Kyi home.

text.p: Burma's military government said it would not allow a large gathering of Aung San Suu Kyi's opposition party at her home on Tuesday, but said a small group had been permitted to go in.

A senior opposition National League for Democracy (NLD) source said only 10 party executive committee members would be allowed into Suu Kyi's house to hold a meeting. The NLD had planned to hold a gathering to mark the anniversary of the party's landslide 1990 election victory which was not recognised by the ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC).

The government spokesman said:"The NLD has not sought permission to hold such a large gathering. If they hold such a meeting at Suu Kyi's house, they will be stopped. Only the party's executive committee members, family members and those living there can go in."
The NLD source said that most discussions for the planned party's seventh anniversary had already been completed on May 26 by those party members who managed to meet in Rangoon.

"Technically the meeting on the occasion of the seventh anniversary was completed successfully and we will continue with our struggle for democracy until we reach the goal even though the SLORC tries all means to stop us," the NLD source said.

He added that the SLORC had detained up to 316 party members, inlcuding about 50 members of parliament, nationwide to thwart the planned special gathering since last week. The SLORC has denied the charge and asked the NLD to prove the detentions.
